item.title: And its former ignorant attachments are fully possessed and perfected. They are cut off, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable…
item.description:
And its former ignorant attachments are fully possessed and perfected. They are cut off, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to exist in the future, without the capacity to arise again. Therefore, a bhikkhu thus endowed is endowed with the supreme intellectual offering. For, bhikkhu, this is the supreme noble intellectual offering, namely the abandonment of all attachments.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 140 – Dhātuvibhaṅgasutta

item.title: Friends, here the Teacher lives in seclusion, but the disciples do not follow the practice of seclusion. The things that the Teacher teaches to be…
item.description:
Friends, here the Teacher lives in seclusion, but the disciples do not follow the practice of seclusion. The things that the Teacher teaches to be abandoned, they do not abandon. And they live in abundance, lazy, leading the way to backsliding, neglecting the burden of seclusion.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 3 – Dhammadāyādasutta

item.title: Or when there is hatred internally, he understands: 'There is hatred in me'; or when there is no hatred internally, he understands: 'There is no…
item.description:
Or when there is hatred internally, he understands: 'There is hatred in me'; or when there is no hatred internally, he understands: 'There is no hatred in me.' And he understands how unarisen hatred arises; and he understands how arisen hatred is abandoned; and he understands how abandoned hatred will not arise in the future.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 22 – Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta

item.title: Household wealth is abandoned, but hard to share in the goal of asceticism. One brings harm to oneself and brings distraction, Like a funeral torch…
item.description:
Household wealth is abandoned, but hard to share in the goal of asceticism.
One brings harm to oneself and brings distraction,
Like a funeral torch that goes to destruction.

Many who wear the yellow robe,
Of evil nature, unrestrained,
By their evil deeds, certainly go to hell.

Better to swallow a red-hot iron ball,
Blazing like a fire,
Than for an immoral, unrestrained person
To eat the country's almsfood.

From: Itivuttaka 91

item.title: Possessing forty qualities, as such is placed in heaven. What forty? He himself abstains from killing living beings, does not encourage others to kill, does…
item.description:
Possessing forty qualities, as such is placed in heaven. What forty? He himself abstains from killing living beings, does not encourage others to kill, does not consent to killing, and does not praise killing; he himself abstains from taking what is not given, does not encourage others to take what is not given, does not consent to taking what is not given, and does not praise taking what is not given; he himself abstains from sexual misconduct, does not encourage others to engage in sexual misconduct, does not consent to sexual misconduct, and does not praise sexual misconduct; he himself does not speak falsely, does not encourage others to speak falsely, does not consent to false speech, and does not praise false speech; he himself abstains from divisive speech, does not encourage others to speak divisively, does not consent to divisive speech, and does not praise divisive speech; he himself does not speak harshly, does not encourage others to speak harshly, does not consent to harsh speech, and does not praise harsh speech; he himself abstains from idle chatter, does not encourage others to speak idly, does not consent to idle chatter, and does not praise idle chatter; he himself is not covetous, does not encourage others to be covetous, does not consent to covetousness, and does not praise covetousness; he himself has no ill-will, does not encourage others to have ill-will, does not consent to ill-will, and does not praise ill-will; he himself has right view, encourages others to have right view, consents to right view, and praises right view. Possessing these forty qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in heaven.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.224

item.title: There are these four occasions, bhikkhus, that, if well developed and well conducted, lead progressively to the destruction of the taints. What four? Hearing the…
item.description:
There are these four occasions, bhikkhus, that, if well developed and well conducted, lead progressively to the destruction of the taints. What four? Hearing the Dhamma at the right time, discussing the Dhamma at the right time, calming at the right time, contemplating at the right time. These four occasions, bhikkhus, if well developed and well conducted, lead progressively to the destruction of the taints.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.147

item.title: This is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen: that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of…
item.description:
This is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen: that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This is impossible. It is possible, bhikkhus, that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. This is possible. This is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen: that a person who has done evil verbal actions... evil mental actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This is impossible. It is possible, bhikkhus, that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. This is possible.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.290

item.title: A learner training, practicing the straight path, In the destruction of evil states is the first knowledge, Next is final knowledge — that final knowledge…
item.description:
A learner training, practicing the straight path,
In the destruction of evil states is the first knowledge,
Next is final knowledge — that final knowledge is unsurpassed.

After that final knowledge, liberation itself,
Liberation knowledge unsurpassed
In the destruction of evil states, the wise.
Here the various fetters are destroyed.

Not the lazy, the fool who knows nothing,
Can attain this unsurpassed Nibbāna,
The complete liberation from all bonds.

From: Itivuttaka 102

item.title: Venerable Sir, if it is indeed difficult for me, following different views, accepting different things, pursuing different goals, following different aims, trained under different methods,…
item.description:
Venerable Sir, if it is indeed difficult for me, following different views, accepting different things, pursuing different goals, following different aims, trained under different methods, to attain purity and liberation, then at least, Venerable Sir, I will place my confidence in the Blessed One, and I will guard that faith well.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 24 – Pāthikasutta

item.title: Whatever fears arise, bhikkhus, all those fears arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Whatever disappointments arise, all those disappointments arise for the foolish,…
item.description:
Whatever fears arise, bhikkhus, all those fears arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Whatever disappointments arise, all those disappointments arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Whatever calamities arise, all those calamities arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Just as, bhikkhus, a spark from a grass hut can burn down a gabled house plastered inside and out, protected from the wind, with bolted doors and shutters — so too, bhikkhus, whatever fears arise, all those fears arise for the foolish, not for the wise; whatever disappointments arise, all those disappointments arise for the foolish, not for the wise; whatever calamities arise, all those calamities arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Thus, bhikkhus, the foolish is full of fear, the wise is without fear. The foolish is full of disappointment, the wise is without disappointment. The foolish is full of calamity, the wise is without calamity. Bhikkhus, there is no fear for the wise, no disappointment for the wise, no calamity for the wise. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves: 'We will become wise and reflective.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 115 – Bahudhātukasutta
